chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hak-Hakam, from Muawiya ibn Wahb, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that a son of his came to him one night and said to him, 'O father, I wish to sleep.'

So he said, 'O my son, say: I testify that there is no god except Allah, and that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is His servant and His Messenger. I seek Refuge with the Magnificence of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Might of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Power of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Majesty of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Authority of Allah. Indeed, Allah is Able over everything.'

And I seek Refuge with the Pardon of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Forgiveness of Allah, and I seek Refuge with the Mercy of Allah, from the evil of the venomous creature and the insect, and from the evil of every animal, small or big, by night or by day, and from the evil of the mischievous of the Jinn and the humans, and from the evil of the mischievous of the Arabs and the non-Arabs, and from the evil of the thunderbolts and the hail. O Allah, send Blessings upon Muhammad, Your servant and Your Messenger.
Muawiya said, 'So the good child would say, 'Good,' during the mention of the Blessed Prophet.' He said, 'Yes, O my son, the good, the blessed.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication to recite before sleeping according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the prophetic tradition of instilling spiritual awareness in children through bedtime supplications, emphasizing the interplay between faith declaration and divine protection. The Imam’s instruction to seek refuge in Allah’s majesty, might, and power reflects the Shia emphasis on utilizing specific divine attributes (Sifat) for spiritual safeguarding against unseen harms. The narrative also underscores the pedagogical value of associating children with the Prophet’s name to evoke reverence and barakah.
